nom: Drunk Elephant E-Rase Milki Micellar Water

segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin, including one managing rosacea, consistently report no stinging, burning, or breakouts, several specifically recommending it as a gentle option for sensitive or reactive skin.
segments.dry: The one reviewer who describes dry skin found the texture too heavy and goopy, leaving an uncomfortable residue rather than the light finish others describe.
segments.combination: Reports from reviewers with combination skin are mixed: one says it works well and hydrates after sports, but another says it made her break out and feel gross on her skin over a couple of weeks of use.

concerns.dehydration: The large majority of reviewers describe the micellar water as hydrating rather than drying, several contrasting it with other makeup removers that leave a tight, dry feeling, and one says it visibly helped skin that had been feeling dry and dull.
concerns.redness: A couple of reviewers say the formula is soothing on irritated or inflamed skin, one noting it calms without any burning sensation.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer credits the ceramide blend with helping support a healthy skin barrier while soothing her skin.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers say it doesn't cause breakouts and a few specifically note clearer skin with use, but two reviewers report new pimples or breakouts appearing after they started using it.

aspects.libelle: A little goes a long way
Cotton pads absorb too much product

extraits.texte: I used it for the first time to remove makeup and it took forever to remove all my makeup. I went throught a lot of cotton pads get my makeup off. I keep using more and more product, hoping that my makeup would finally be removed, but no. I had to use a different makeup remover product to remove my makeup. The next morning, I woke up with small break outs on my face. For the price of this product, it is not worth it. There are cheaper miceller water products.

I was extremely disappointed in this product. I'm an avid makeup wearer and liberal double-cleanser. I tried this out as my first step in my nightly regimen and found myself going through so much cotton to get my makeup off compared to other brands (La Roche Posay and IT Cosmetics). The texture was goopy and extremely heavy even for a dry skin person like myself. It left an uncomfortable texture behind so I wouldn't recommend this for people who want a no-rinse cleanser either. Also was not a fan of the scent. Smells like stale Play-Doh.

extraits.titre: not for me, I have combination skin
extraits.texte: my skin was under control for a long time and I decided to try this and the last couple weeks I keep getting pimples and my skin feels gross when i use it... its a nice smooth texture. but you have to use a lot to get it working. it's not the worst and has good ingredients, but doesn't help me sadly. I have to go back to to regular micellar water that's more clear

extraits.titre: I use this multiple times a day as a skin refresher
extraits.texte: Not only do I use it, but I've gotten my 14 year-old son to use it as well. He is Ethiopian and has combination skin. It works great and he loves how it cleans and hydrates after sports.

Because of this micellar water, I actually have started washing my face at night for the first time in my life. It is so easy to use and it doesn't irritate my rosacea. A bottle lasts a long time, too.

One of the best micellar waters out there. 1. Affordable 2. Removes all makeup like charm 3. The quantity you use is so little to remove a lot 4. does not give me pimples since i have sensitive skin. 5. is not sticky or slick feeling gifted by drunkelephant

The E-Rase Milki Micellar Water is thicker than your typical micellar water. It feels hydrating and removes makeup very easily without any irritation. It removed mascara and eyeliner with ease. It can also be used to refresh the skin, it contains a 3 ceramide blend & wild watermelon seed oil to help hydrate. It feels soothing to my skin and helps to support a healthy skin barrier. Gifted by Drunkelephant
